evidence: The disk comment said 'Three images per run' and sized off ~142 MB of baked assets beside a four-row matrix with a ~3 GiB leg, and publish had no timeout-minutes while cancel-in-progress is false; b367bdb rewrote the comment against the matrix and added timeout-minutes: 60.
guidance_note: When adding a row to a build matrix, grep the same workflow for every comment that counts or sizes the legs (disk, RAM, timeouts) and restate or delete each in the same commit.

evidence: The class docstring makes _speaking the sole guard against cross-voice corruption and no test exercised overlapping speak calls; the agent added a stub-model two-thread test and reports it fails with the lock removed.
guidance_note: When a docstring names a lock as the only thing preventing a silent wrong answer, ship a stub-driven concurrency test that fails with the lock removed in the same PR.

evidence: _cloned read model.conds lazily for builtin while every reference-speaker clone overwrites it via prepare_conditionals, and voices() treats operator order as meaningful, so CHATTERBOX_SPEAKERS=alice,builtin made builtin speak as alice; fix captures builtin before the loop, with a test confirmed to fail pre-fix.
guidance_note: When a loop body reads a mutable slot that other iterations of the same loop write, capture the value before the loop and pass it in.

evidence: The compat risk is answered by the PR itself: CI runs uv run --all-extras against one lock resolved for all four extras on 3.13 and is green, and requires-python cannot be scoped per extra; the missing rationale was real and b367bdb added the numpy<2 vs numpy>=2.0.2 explanation.
guidance_note: When raising a project-wide floor for one dependency's sake, write the resolving constraint beside the pin in the same commit.

evidence: b367bdb rewrote the disk-sizing comment for the fourth leg but left the RAM comment saying 'all three legs share one Docker daemon on 2 cpu and 7.9GB' (its replacement is visible in 4274047), and the bake really peaks at a measured 6.68 GiB; the agent fixed it once in the workflow comment rather than copying the figure into the Dockerfile.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale leg-count comment in a workflow, search that file for every other sentence that counts the legs and fix them all in the same commit.

evidence: Same three-leg RAM comment that the F1 fix's disk-comment rewrite left standing; 4274047 replaces 'all three legs' with every-leg wording plus the measured 4.69/6.68 GiB figure and the concurrency consequence, and the agent stated it could not verify the runner (registry unreachable) rather than claiming to.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale leg-count comment in a workflow, search that file for every other sentence that counts the legs and fix them all in the same commit.

evidence: The agent measured two live models at 8.11 GiB resident / 10.10 peak, confirming the premise, then moved both config refusals above from_local so they need no model at all, which is a better fix than restructuring tests. Flag is a false positive: b367bdb touched only workflow comments and the pyproject comment, while the two-model order test is original PR code.
guidance_note: Before writing a test that opens a multi-GiB model, check whether the behavior under test needs the model at all, and put the cheap refusals ahead of the expensive load.

evidence: The '~300 MB' comment was stale (4274047 shows it), but the timeout risk was measured false: 10m49s and 12m20s with chatterbox against a 30-minute bound. The F1 fix revised publish's timeout and size comment without sweeping the tests job's comments in the same file.
guidance_note: When an engine's asset size changes by an order of magnitude, grep every workflow for the old asset-size and duration claims, not just the job the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: The tests.yml '~300 MB / about a minute' comment was stale and fixed in 4274047; the opt-in gate was rightly refused because the gate measured 12m20s against 30 with chatterbox fully exercised and the suite's stated policy is that skips read as passes.
guidance_note: When an engine's asset size changes by an order of magnitude, grep every workflow for the old asset-size and duration claims, not just the job the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: The agent quoted the installed library's prepare_conditionals ending 'self.conds = Conditionals(t3_cond, s3gen_ref_dict)', a rebind rather than an in-place write, so the reference captured by the F3 fix cannot be corrupted; it documented that dependency at the capture and declined a real-model test. The finding exists only because the F3 fix relied on reference semantics without saying so.
guidance_note: When a fix's correctness rests on a third-party library's assignment semantics, read that library source and name the assumption in a comment in the same commit.

evidence: The table row 'CPU (12 cores) 7.62 - 33.3' contradicted the paragraph attributing 7.62-33.3 to 4 threads; relabelled to 'CPU (12 cores, 4 threads)'. Flag is a false positive: 4274047 touched only workflow comments and the table is original PR content.

evidence: F7 explicitly listed test_a_timestamps_request_is_refused_rather_than_answered_with_invented_numbers as a fourth two-model case, and the F7 fix handled the other three; the agent conceded 'I fixed three siblings last round and missed this one'.
guidance_note: When a finding enumerates sibling instances, fix every listed one and then grep the file (here for chatterbox_prepared(...).open()) for unlisted ones before replying.

evidence: The F6 fix wrote 'size this runner before clearing chatterbox to publish', which read as a control the workflow does not have; the gate itself is a deliberate human git push gitea master, and an exclude: would break the matrix == ENGINES invariant tests/test_workflow.py holds (cited in the F1 reply). The agent declined the gate and fixed the wording.

evidence: Nothing in the packet shows torch's x86-64 baseline or the runner's CPU, so whether v2 suffices is unsettled; keeping the measured floor and generalizing the NumPy-only error message was a reasonable split. evidence: test_the_engine_speaks_on_the_device_the_deployment_named asserted only that short utterances yield audio; renamed to match the body. Flag is a false positive: ab83d48 touched pyproject, uv.lock and the version-bound test, not this test's name or body.
guidance_note: When a test body is rewritten or moved, re-read its name against what it now asserts.

narrative: A large engine addition whose real bugs (builtin ordering, two-model memory, missing lock test) were caught in round 0 and fixed well. Most later rounds were spent on stale copies of measured facts (leg counts, RAM peak, RTF range, asset size) that each fix corrected at the reviewer's pointed site and nowhere else, until the agent turned the copies into a scanning drift test in round 3. Round 3 consisted only of fix-caused drift findings; round 4 found one more divider made stale by the F7 fix. The review hit the 5-round cap with the last push unreviewed, and ab83d48 reverted torch CPU-index routing added earlier in the PR without a finding prompting it.
guidance_observations: Every measured number in this PR was hand-copied into 3-5 files, and each review round found one more copy; a single source plus a repo-wide scan test written with the first fix would have closed round 3 entirely.
The agent measured before deciding (two-model RSS, CI wall time) and used those measurements to reject an opt-in gate and an unnecessary timeout bump, which made the pushbacks checkable.
The PR ended at the review round cap with the head commit unreviewed, so the final fixes (F19, F20) merged without a review pass.

evidence: The reviewer asked for the new from_local assumption to join the inventory in test_the_upper_bound_..._is_there's docstring (mirrored in the pyproject comment ab83d48 wrote) that a uv lock --upgrade reviewer reads; the agent documented it only in _releasing_state_dict's docstring and argued against a runtime check nobody proposed, so the bump-time inventory stays incomplete. 'Silently' was overstated, since a cleared dict being re-read would likely fail loudly.
guidance_note: When adding a new dependency on library internals, add it to the existing pin-bump inventory (the pyproject comment and its test docstring) in the same commit, not only beside the code.

evidence: The agent named specific conformance properties run against the real model through _open (longer text makes more audio, measured samples account for every sample), contradicting 'only assert len(audio) > 0', and the stand-in test asserts the copy is complete before the clear; the packet does not show those test bodies, but the line-numbered citations are specific and the remaining version risk is the F1 topic.

narrative: A small memory-peak fix that monkeypatches T3.load_state_dict for a bounded window. Round 0 raised a version-coupling concern and a test-coverage concern; the agent documented the assumption in the function docstring and correctly rebutted the coverage claim. Round 1 found nothing.
guidance_observations: The agent answered F1 by rebutting a runtime check the reviewer never asked for, and so missed the reviewer's actual request to extend the existing pin-bump inventory.
